## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Puññakiriyavatthu Sutta* (Iti 60; It 3.11, PTS It 51) is a discourse in the *Tikanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text briefly sets forth the three grounds or bases for meritorious activity (*puññakiriyavatthu*) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records nineteen modern translations across sixteen languages, including an English rendering by Bhikkhu Sujato under the title *Grounds for Making Merit* [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral identifies a full parallel to the discourse in the Chinese Buddhist canon at T 765.136 (福業事) [SuttaCentral]. Passage-level parallels are found in the *Metta Sutta* of the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 22) and in the *Ekottarika-āgama* (EĀ 10.7, 施福), while a resembling discourse is preserved in the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 8.36, *Puññakiriyavatthusutta*) [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus corroborates extensive text reuse with AN 8.36, sharing 21 matching passages amounting to 2,464 characters (most notably §0.3–2.4 aligned with AN 8.36 §36.0.2–36.2.1) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus additionally documents shared passages with the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* (§2.1–2.3 aligned with §345_4–345_5), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, and several adjacent discourses within the *Itivuttaka* that share formulaic opening and closing segments (such as Iti 64, Iti 65, and Iti 61) [DharmaNexus].

None of the surveyed secondary literature passages discuss Iti 60 directly; rather, occurrences of *puññakiriyavatthu* in the search results treat the doctrinal category of the three (or ten) bases of merit generically or focus on AN 8.36 and later Abhidhamma and commentarial classifications.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
